summary.title: Learn to Create D3.js Data Visualizations by Example
summary.one_liner: You learn how D3.js maps data to HTML, SVG and CSS through examples of bar charts, a contribution chart, line charts, scales, and an animated flight visualization with transitions.
keywords: how to make charts with javascript
takeaways: D3 maps data to HTML and SVG elements using selections, appending elements per data point via enter().append().
Scales (linear and time) convert data values into pixel coordinates, with optional padding on the output range.
SVG basics (circle, text, path, line) are the building blocks; d3 line generators create path data from x/y points.
Enter, update and exit patterns plus transition() with duration and ease let you animate changing data frame by frame.
summary.summary: The article is a hands-on overview of D3.js, starting with a bar chart built from divs and a GitHub-style contribution chart using color interpolation. It then introduces SVG primitives, circles and text bound to object data, and a line chart using D3's path generator. Scales are covered next, showing how linear and time scales map data domains to pixel ranges with padding. The final sections build an animated flight visualization using a render loop, enter/update/exit selections, and transitions, and it points to the D3 gallery and Scott Murray's tutorials for further study.
